analysis: Examined CHANGELOG.md base-side units 3159-3650, which are historical release notes (release pipeline, dev-branch lane, threat-review tooling, cache, Autopilot, erasure and similar topics) and fall outside the changed ranges. The only change in this file is head lines 11-39 (range_map_complete=true). Those lines add a v0.10.10 candidate section describing the `darkbloom waitlist` command and the new approval gate on `darkbloom sandbox setup` and new non-local `darkbloom cluster` pairs. It is documentation only; no code is visible in this batch. The truncated patch excerpt ends at 'If the coordinator does not offer waitlists yet, both new setups go on as in 0.' That implies a fail-open fallback when the coordinator lacks waitlist support. This is a business and availability gate, not a security control in TB-013 or TB-014. T-061 (tampered installer) and T-062 (GPU-limit root job) concern installer integrity and local confirmation; a waitlist approval is not described as one of their mitigations. Integration should confirm that the implementation does not let coordinator waitlist responses (TB-002, a trusted coordinator) influence installer URLs, the commands run as the owner (A-019), or privileged gpu-limit actions (A-020). It should also confirm that approval text containing 'the command that starts the feature' is displayed only, never executed. No regression was identified from the changelog text alone. The waitlist/approval implementation source was not supplied, which is a coverage limit.
